name: Le Tigre
label: Mr. Lady
lede: Kathleen Hanna named Le Tigre in 1994, four years before it had a member. When Bikini Kill ended, she finally put a band behind the name, and it played dance floors for the next quarter century.

eras.title: A band name with no band
eras.text: Kathleen Hanna keeps a running list of bands that don't exist. When Bikini Kill ends in 1998, one of them gets members.

years.h: Hanna dreams up Le Tigre years before it plays a note
years.p: Around 1994 [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] starts inventing hypothetical bands. Le Tigre is one of them, and it's the one she ends up building.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album)
years.h: Bikini Kill ends, and the Julie Ruin solo songs get a live band
years.p: Hanna asks Johanna Fateman, whom she met at a Bikini Kill show, and the artist [[Sadie Benning|ad77bd6f-90e3-439d-b990-bfed508686a8]] to play her solo material on stage.
years.xp:
Hanna and Fateman had already played together in a band called the Troublemakers, and Hanna had worked with Benning on video for her solo album as [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]]. The plan was a live format for the solo songs. It became a band instead.

The trio traded song ideas on cassette while Benning was based in Chicago, then signed with Mr. Lady Records. Hanna called the label "a logical choice" for its political commitment.

eras.title: Drum machines and a slide projector
eras.text: The first record comes out on a feminist label started with $35, and the line-up reshuffles around what touring demands.

years.h: JD Samson joins as a roadie and advances the slides by hand
years.p: [[JD Samson|fd42790a-2d28-4564-9da9-9b3686597ec8]] comes on the crew in September 1999. There's no budget for automation, so Samson clicks through the slide projector during the set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Le Tigre comes out on Mr. Lady, a label that began with $35
years.p: Chris Stamey of the dB's produces; the sound is Alesis drum machines, a Farfisa organ, samplers and turntables.
years.xp:
Fateman described the gear choice as "girl-punk scorn for that particular strain of male expertise" tied to electronic music. Mr. Lady was founded by Tammy Rae Carland and Kaia Wilson, and Wilson has said it started with "$35 and a lotta...faith".

Robert Christgau wrote that Hanna "reinvents punk again." Spin gave it 9/10, and Pitchfork put it 43rd on its 2022 list of the best 1990s albums.

years.h: Deceptacon opens the record, and the crowd learns the dance
years.p: The opener riffs on Barry Mann's 1961 single "Who Put the Bomp". At shows it spawns a crowd choreography called the aerobicon.

years.h: Hot Topic reads like a syllabus you can dance to
years.p: The song name-checks women and LGBTQ+ artists and activists, and Hanna compared it to a college syllabus. Its sister track, My My Metrocard, takes on New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani's quality-of-life policing.

years.cap: Le Tigre at the Volcano Room, Indianapolis, September 22, 2000
q: JD added an undeniable flair and charisma to the live show.
years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album) · Wikipedia: Sadie Benning
years.h: Benning can't tour, so Samson becomes the third member
years.p: Sadie Benning steps back to focus on filmmaking, and JD Samson goes from roadie to permanent member.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page dates the change to 2000 and says Benning left to focus on film. The album page says Benning couldn't tour behind the record. Benning's own page gives 2001.

Benning went on to a career in video, painting and sculpture, with work in the collections of MoMA and the Whitney.

eras.title: Feminist Sweepstakes and a festival fight
eras.text: A second record with a new line-up, and a very public argument about who a women's festival is for.

years.h: Feminist Sweepstakes gets cut in Chapel Hill with Samson on board
years.p: Hanna, Fateman and Samson record with Chris Stamey at Modern Recording. It's the first album by the trio.
years.xp:
F.Y.R. draws on Shulamith Firestone's The Dialectic of Sex, and Dyke March 2001 is built from field recordings of New York's Dyke March. Keep on Livin' turned up again in the 2019 Jessica Jones finale.

Metacritic lists it at 78/100, and Christgau and Entertainment Weekly both gave it an A-. Samson has said the title came from imagining what a feminist Easter basket might look like.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Le Tigre plays Michigan Womyn's Music Festival and takes the heat
years.p: The festival's womyn-born womyn policy excluded trans women. Per Wikipedia, the band and the Butchies got criticism and death threats for playing it in 2001 and 2005.
years.xp:
Mr. Lady Records took its own backlash in 1999 for backing the festival, with Camp Trans and others boycotting. Wilson said at the time that transgender and transsexual people are an important part of the queer community.

Samson, who identifies as genderqueer, later said publicly (2013, on Tumblr) that they would not take part until all self-identified women were welcome. The festival closed in 2015.

years.h: Wordy Rappinghood pulls in Chicks on Speed and Tina Weymouth
years.p: [[Chicks on Speed|4da58f86-c7fb-4837-9ef5-423f122d2d15]] cover a Tom Tom Club song with Le Tigre, Miss Kittin, Kevin Blechdom, ADULT.'s Nicola Kuperus and Tom Tom Club's Tina Weymouth. It hits number 5 on the Belgian Dance Chart and 66 in the UK.

eras.title: A feminist band on a Universal label
eras.text: Tired of the same circuit, Le Tigre tries a Universal subsidiary and finds out what happens.

years.big: "It was time for a change for us."
years.src: Wikipedia: This Island (Le Tigre album) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band)
years.h: Le Tigre signs to Strummer, a Universal Records subsidiary
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]], on the move after years of touring.
years.xp: Hanna also said she wanted feminist perspectives in mainstream spaces, and that she was bored doing the same thing over and over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Mr. Lady Records
years.h: Mr. Lady shuts down, so Le Tigre reissues its own back catalog
years.p: The band starts Le Tigre Records to keep the first two albums in print, distributed by Touch and Go.

years.h: This Island, the major-label record they made at home
years.p: Home studios around Manhattan, mostly Pro Tools, with Nick Sansano producing and Ric Ocasek producing one track, Tell You Now.
years.xp:
Touring money paid for the home studios, so there were no studio deadlines and no label in the room. New Kicks samples Susan Sarandon and Al Sharpton from New York's 2003 anti-war protests.

It peaked at number 130 on the Billboard 200 and had sold 90,000 copies by 2008. Metacritic has it at 66/100.

years.cap: Le Tigre at Roskilde Festival, Denmark, June 30, 2005
years.h: Le Tigre plays TKO on Conan
years.p: The band takes TKO to late-night TV in 2005, and the footage survives online.

years.cap: Le Tigre at Roskilde Festival, Denmark
years.h: After This Island, the band goes quiet
years.p: Touring exhaustion and three separate projects put Le Tigre on ice in August 2007.

eras.title: Hiatus, with cameos
eras.text: No band, but the songs keep turning up: on a pop record, at a Pussy Riot set, in a documentary.

years.h: Christina Aguilera calls Le Tigre in to produce My Girls
years.p: [[Christina Aguilera|b202beb7-99bd-47e7-8b72-195c8d72ebdd]] brings the band in, with [[Peaches|270acfee-1fbe-413e-a0a8-6a35a8b3b66c]] guesting, for a track on Bionic. Hanna's next band is [[The Julie Ruin|357ffd02-384f-4dbd-abcd-5f1bcb616ef9]].

yt: Deceptacon clip, Who Took the Bomp?
years.h: Who Took the Bomp? puts the 2004 tour on screen
years.p: Oscilloscope's tour documentary Who Took the Bomp? Le Tigre on Tour screens at San Francisco's Frameline festival.

years.h: Fateman and Samson play Deceptacon with Pussy Riot
years.p: At a Vice magazine concert in 2014 the pair perform it with [[Pussy Riot|631e3bc5-428a-432b-87f7-5d357a007fc0]]. The two groups reunite in 2015 to make material for Netflix's House of Cards.

eras.title: Back, and a lawsuit
eras.text: A campaign song, a copyright fight over the debut's opener, then the first tour in 18 years.

years.h: I'm With Her backs Hillary Clinton
years.p: After a September announcement of a one-off, Le Tigre releases the song with a video supporting Clinton's presidential campaign.

years.src: Wikipedia: Le Tigre (band) · Wikipedia: Le Tigre (album)
years.h: Barry Mann says Deceptacon owes him a song
years.p: Mann, writer of 1961's Who Put the Bomp, claims infringement. Hanna and Fateman countersue in October and settle in November.
years.xp: Hanna and Fateman argued that the song's use of the bomp line was transformative critique, not copying. The case ended in a confidential settlement agreement with no public admission of liability.

years.h: This Ain't No Picnic is Le Tigre's first festival slot back
years.p: Announced in December 2021, it returns the band to a big stage in 2022.

years.cap: Le Tigre on the 2023 tour, c. 2023
yt: Hot Topic, Albert Hall Manchester, June 2023
years.h: The first tour in 18 years mostly sells out
years.p: European and North American dates go up in January. By June the band is at Manchester's Albert Hall, playing Hot Topic.
